points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree, i.e. a tree in which each node has at most two children (left and right). Accept 'binary tree' or an equivalent description of the at-most-two-children structure.
States the ordering property on the left: for a node, the left child (or all values in the left subtree) is smaller / less than the parent node's value.
States the ordering property on the right: for a node, the right child (or all values in the right subtree) is greater / larger than the parent node's value.

States that the ordering property holds for every node in the tree (i.e. it applies recursively at each node, not just at the root). Accept 'for any node', 'at every node', 'recursively throughout the tree' or equivalent.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all four ideas: it is a binary tree, left values are smaller than the parent, right values are larger than the parent, and this holds at every node. An answer that gives only the ordering rule without saying it is a binary tree, or that gives only one side of the ordering, earns the corresponding points only. An answer that describes an ordinary binary tree with no ordering property, or reverses the ordering (left larger, right smaller), earns no marks for P2-P4.
